name: Sir George Etherege
credit: No confirmed portrait sourced for this archive.
bio: Sir George Etherege (1636–1692) was an English Restoration dramatist, author of The Comical Revenge, She Would if She Could and The Man of Mode. He served as a diplomat at Constantinople and Ratisbon, and wrote a handful of polished songs and lyrics.

The poem here is the one printed under his name in Frederick Locker's Lyra Elegantiarum (London: E. Moxon, 1867), an anthology of vers de société and vers d'occasion by deceased authors; the texts follow that first edition.

poems.title: Ye happy swains, whose hearts are free
poems.author: Sir George Etherege
poems.collection: Lyra Elegantiarum, ed. Frederick Locker (London: E. Moxon, 1867)
poems.text:
Ye happy swains, whose hearts are free
From Love's imperial chain.
Take warning, and be taught by me,
T' avoid th' enchanting pain.

Fatal the wolves to trembling flocks—
Fierce winds to blossoms prove—
To careless seamen, hidden rocks—
To human quiet, love.

Then fly the Fair, if bliss you prize;
The snake's beneath the flower:
Who ever gazed on beauteous eyes,
And tasted quiet more?

How faithless is the lover's joy!
How constant is his care!
The kind with falsehood do destroy,
The cruel with despair.
